challenge: Employee remittance gaps are timing artefacts
adversarial_hypothesis: Apparent gaps could vanish after timing arrears base-definition and perimeter adjustments
evidence_required: payroll withholding totals;CGA worker-quota revenue;timing adjustments;arrears corrections
current_evidence: Legal worker-rate history is registered but payroll and revenue split are missing
notes: No remittance-gap claim should be stated beyond the registered missing-input limitation

challenge: Employer gaps come from incorrect legal rates
adversarial_hypothesis: Alleged gaps could reflect applying the wrong employer rate or treating an economic benchmark as legal debt
evidence_required: legal employer rates by class;payroll bases;recorded CGA employer revenue;economic benchmark definition
current_evidence: Legal-rate distinction is registered and the economic benchmark is explicitly not a legal debt; payroll and revenue values are missing
notes: Legal-rate confusion is controlled conceptually but quantitative gap tests remain blocked

challenge: State transfers were intended historical financing
adversarial_hypothesis: State Budget transfers may be the intended financing mechanism rather than evidence of underpayment or loss
evidence_required: CGA component ledger;legal transfer rules;annual State transfer classification
current_evidence: CGA 2011 balance extract is registered but detailed transfer-purpose components are missing
notes: State transfers must not be interpreted as non-compliance without legal and accounting classification

challenge: The 2006 RGSS effect is smaller than claimed
adversarial_hypothesis: Post-2006 public-worker reallocation could be materially smaller under observed cohorts payroll bases or RGSS pension-only rates
evidence_required: public-worker new-entrant cohorts;contribution bases;RGSS rates;pension-only decomposition
current_evidence: Lei 60/2005 establishes CGA closure but cohort counts contribution bases and rates are missing
notes: No magnitude claim can be made until the reallocation inputs are registered

challenge: Combined deficits depend on perimeter choices
adversarial_hypothesis: Sign and magnitude of combined balances could change when CGA RGSS FEFSS bank and consolidation perimeters are altered
evidence_required: RGSS/previdential balances;CGA components;FEFSS flows;flow-of-funds bridge rows
current_evidence: Flow-of-funds bridge now marks consolidation and bank/BPN rows but RGSS and FEFSS annual flows remain missing
notes: Perimeter dependence is structurally guarded but not numerically resolved

challenge: The 2011 bank transfer was balanced once specific State financing is included
adversarial_hypothesis: Specific State financing may offset bank-special-regime pension payments and eliminate a Social Security loss interpretation
evidence_required: annual State transfers;pension expenditure;administrative cost;asset drawdown;investment income;timing adjustments
current_evidence: The 2012 official audit reports EUR 516.0m financing and EUR 516.0m pension payments; post-2012 lifecycle components remain missing
notes: The 2012 cash identity is reconciled but does not settle lifecycle cost or bank-level net positions

challenge: The bank transfer appears adverse only under selectively chosen discount rates
adversarial_hypothesis: Adverse conclusions may depend on selectively low discount rates instead of a full sensitivity range
evidence_required: pension cash-flow schedule;mortality assumptions;legal 4 percent valuation;2 to 6 percent sensitivity outputs
current_evidence: The 2 to 6 percent sensitivity grid is registered but cannot be populated without cash-flow and demographic schedules
notes: Discount-rate selectivity is a mandatory test but currently lacks the cash-flow basis

challenge: The bank transfer remains adverse under conservative assumptions and full legal financing
adversarial_hypothesis: A fully financed conservative lifecycle reconstruction could still show the transfer was adverse to public finances
evidence_required: full pension cash-flow path;asset composition;asset income;State financing;gross-debt classification;retained bank liabilities
current_evidence: Registered rows show 2011 asset receipt and 2012 pension financing but not asset composition lifecycle costs or retained-liability values
notes: The current evidence cannot support either an adverse or benign lifecycle classification
